source_row_verbatim: The system shall create and maintain a canonical service record with technical and business owners, criticality, environment, lifecycle state, essential functions, objectives, and certification status.
Versioned service record and audit event.
The system shall detect missing, stale, conflicting, or unverified ownership and criticality data and shall prevent production certification while required fields remain unresolved.
Finding, certification decision, and exception record.
The system shall support provider resource aliases without changing the canonical service identity and shall retain source, confidence, and observation timestamps for each mapping.
The system shall represent services, resources, models, datasets, identities, locations, failure domains, controls, vendors, and recovery targets as typed Neo4j nodes and relationships.
Graph schema version and constraint report.
The system shall record direction, dependency type, criticality, synchrony, fallback, provenance, confidence, freshness, owner, and propagation behavior for every decision-relevant relationship.
The system shall calculate bounded blast-radius and upstream-cause traversals from a declared graph revision and shall return the paths, exclusions, confidence, and freshness used in the result.
Query result hash and graph revision.
The system shall reconcile catalog, provider inventory, and Neo4j topology; classify divergence; and place affected decisions into Unknown when context no longer satisfies policy.

The system shall enforce the canonical node registry and controlled relationship vocabulary in Section 5.2.7 and Appendix M; unsupported labels, relationship names, directions, properties, or schema versions shall be rejected or quarantined.
Ontology registry, rejected mutation, and migration report.

The system shall map technical dependencies to customer journeys, journey steps, essential functions, customer segments, SLOs, controls, impacts, outcomes, and outcome measures using versioned, attributable relationships.
End-to-end graph fixture and traversal test.
Witness paths from technical source to customer and organizational outcome.

The system shall distinguish observed, estimated, forecast, and bounded impacts; deduplicate overlapping paths and populations; and retain method, inputs, window, unit, assumptions, exclusions, confidence, graph revision, and supersession history.
Impact fixture, overlap, correction, and late-evidence tests.
Impact Calculation record and deterministic replay result.

The system shall evaluate candidate recovery paths against the declared failure scenario, correlation domains, target health, capacity, compatibility, evidence qualification, test status, expiry, and policy tolerances and shall return certification status with witness and rejection paths.
Recovery Path Certification and recertification event.

The system shall bind material impact, fallback, authorization, and validation decisions to an immutable graph revision and action-relevant subgraph digest and shall require re-evaluation when a material graph delta occurs.
Graph delta classification and reauthorization decision.

The system shall preserve canonical identity, provenance, qualification, freshness, contradiction, reconciliation, revision, query identifier, parameters, result digest, and witness paths sufficient to reproduce every consequential graph result.
Independent decision replay and integrity test.
Reconstructed graph result and integrity report.
The system shall ingest required metrics, logs, traces, changes, security events, incidents, experiments, and AI-lifecycle evidence from approved sources.
The system shall validate schema, provenance, timestamp, tenant, environment, identity, and data classification before accepting an event for decision use.
The system shall normalize provider-specific evidence into the canonical event contract while preserving the original provider identifier, unit, value, and drill-down reference.
Normalized event and raw evidence reference.
The system shall deduplicate, order where required, correlate, and enrich events with service, deployment, model, objective, and graph context.

The system shall store each production rule with an owner, rationale, scope, inputs, condition, output, precedence, suppression, cooldown, tests, evidence requirements, effective dates, and rollback version.
The system shall evaluate deterministic detection, propagation, state, recommendation, authorization-input, validation, and adaptation rules using versioned context.
Explanation tree and rule execution trace.
The system shall resolve conflicts using documented precedence and shall produce Unknown rather than unsupported certainty when material evidence conflicts or is stale.
The system shall maintain Normal, Guarded, Elevated, Critical, and Unknown states for each UACRF layer and the overall service.
Current state and immutable transition history.
The system shall explain every active state using source evidence, rule versions, graph paths, service context, suppressions, confidence, and outstanding validation.
The system shall evaluate every candidate action against environment, criticality, action risk, scope, reversibility, confidence, separation of duties, maintenance state, and regulatory constraints.
Policy input, decision, bundle version, and reason.
The system shall return one of deny, recommend, approval required, or preauthorized and shall prevent the rule engine or an ML model from bypassing that decision.
Enforcement log and denied bypass attempt.
The system shall route approval to eligible roles, enforce expiry and separation of duties, capture rationale, and support rejection or requests for additional evidence.
The system shall implement controlled break-glass approval with stronger authentication, mandatory reason, limited duration, immediate notification, and retrospective review.
The system shall execute approved runbooks through durable, idempotent, timeout-bounded, retry-aware, and compensatable workflows.
Workflow event history and idempotency result.
The system shall invoke only allowlisted provider-adapter operations against policy-approved targets and shall reject arbitrary cloud API or shell execution.
The system shall validate technical health, SLO restoration, data integrity, security posture, and AI behavior as applicable after every consequential action.
The system shall hold the service in its current or more restrictive state until the required stable observation window succeeds; otherwise it shall roll back or escalate according to the workflow.
The system shall create an immutable evidence bundle that reconstructs inputs, context, graph revision, rule or model, policy, approval, execution, validation, and outcome.
The system shall support authorized search and export by service, incident, decision, action, experiment, time, provider, and control without modifying retained evidence.
Search result and export audit event.
The system shall link incidents and experiments to findings, root causes, action items, owners, due dates, proposed changes, verification tests, and closure evidence.
The system shall not classify a lesson as implemented until an approved rule, policy, runbook, architecture, model, control, or test change is deployed and verified.
The system shall provide environment and service onboarding workflows with discovery, ownership, graph, telemetry, objective, runbook, policy, test, and certification gates.
The system shall identify deltas when a new resource, dependency, model, data source, action, provider capability, or service version changes the certified baseline.

The initial commercial release shall implement the approved Critical Journey Resilience Assessment boundary and shall prevent unlicensed, unvalidated, or unreleased Control, Recover, Evidence, Quantitative, or Adaptive capabilities from appearing as generally available.
Approved product-boundary register and release manifest.

The system shall record target segment, buyer, champion, funded problem, critical journey, current tools, security constraints, procurement path, success measures, and disqualification reasons for every design partner or pilot.

The system shall lock each paid pilot to an approved service population, provider boundary, failure scenario, recovery path, evidence outputs, responsibilities, exclusions, duration, acceptance measures, and change-control process.
Signed pilot charter, scope version, and acceptance record.

The system shall baseline and measure time to determine impact, time to authorize, time to validated recovery where applicable, dependency gaps, recovery-path deficiencies, manual evidence effort, assessment effort, and customer acceptance for each pilot.
Pilot value report with source references and limitations.

The system shall calculate protected-service, provider-connection, assessment-unit, certified-workflow, evidence-retention, and enabled-intelligence usage without duplicating aliases or deleting retained evidence when entitlement changes.
Meter replay, alias, and entitlement-expiry tests.
Meter ledger, invoice export, and reconciliation report.

The customer onboarding workflow shall assign owner, dependency, access, evidence, validation, and approval responsibilities; record entry and exit criteria for every stage; and prevent production certification while mandatory customer or UACRF tasks remain unresolved.
Responsibility matrix, stage evidence, and certification decision.

Every external product, resilience, compliance, certification, prediction, savings, and autonomy claim shall reference approved wording, supported evidence, applicable product version, limitations, owner, review date, and withdrawal status.

The system shall support implementation plans, success measures, quarterly value reviews, certification renewals, expansion decisions, support health, renewal evidence, and orderly offboarding for contracted customers.
Customer success plan, value history, and completion certificate.

The system shall record gate criteria, accountable approver, required evidence, decision, conditions, expiry, and reopened status for problem validation, MVP, paid pilot, subscription, Control, Recover, Adaptive, sector expansion, and provider expansion.
Gate omission, expiry, and reopen tests.

The system shall attribute implementation labor, platform consumption, support effort, partner cost, contracted revenue, discounts, and expansion to each pilot or customer sufficiently to evaluate gross margin, payback, and services dependency.
The system shall plan, authorize, execute, observe, abort, validate, and retain evidence for controlled fault experiments.
Experiment plan, event history, and report.
The system shall enforce experiment blast-radius limits, stop conditions, protected periods, target allowlists, communications, and recovery readiness.

The system shall present current state, reasons, evidence freshness, dependency impact, proposed actions, authority requirements, workflow status, test status, and unresolved adaptations for an authorized service.
The system shall provide accessible APIs and events for catalog, graph queries, findings, decisions, approvals, workflows, evidence, onboarding, experiments, and administration.
The system shall calculate calibrated layer and systemic scores with parameter provenance, uncertainty, sensitivity, and an explicit mapping back to Core states.
The system shall retain observed outcomes needed to estimate thresholds, propagation parameters, error costs, and forecast performance without allowing a score to override fixed policy.
Calibration dataset manifest and policy result.
The system shall support governed models for anomaly detection, incident prediction, cause ranking, blast-radius estimation, and remediation recommendation in shadow or advisory mode.
Model card, evaluation report, and inference log.
The system shall promote a model to bounded automation only after safety, utility, calibration, drift, explanation, rollback, and human-authority gates are approved.

When collaborative agents are enabled, the system shall seal a case manifest containing qualified evidence, graph revision, policy version, objectives, constraints, assignments, deadline, and integrity digest before agent execution.

Each agent finding, proposal, and dissent shall identify the producer, role, model, prompt, retrieval sources, tools, authority grant, evidence, graph and policy versions, assumptions, confidence, time, digest, and signature.
The system shall retain material dissent independently from proposals and shall not permit a coordinator, summary, or majority result to remove it.

The system shall arbitrate eligible proposals through a versioned deterministic rule bundle and shall route blocking dissent, a substantive tie, or missing mandatory roles to human review or a policy block.
Signed Arbitration Record and replay digest.

Agents shall use short-lived, audience-bound, tenant- and environment-scoped tool grants and shall have no provider credentials, approval authority, evidence-qualification authority, policy-write authority, or direct execution path.
Agent grant and tool invocation ledger.

The agent runtime shall isolate retrieved content from instructions, enforce tool and egress allowlists, classify data, limit time and cost, detect injection attempts, and fail closed on invalid or stale context.
The system shall define deadlines, mandatory roles, attempt identities, duplicate handling, canonical ordering, partial-agent failure behavior, and idempotent tool invocation.
Timeout, duplicate, late-output, and partial-failure tests.
Each agent role shall pass offline, shadow, and advisory evaluations for factuality, evidence citation, safety, reproducibility, injection resistance, latency, and cost before governed collaboration.
Authorized humans shall be able to reject, narrow, defer, or replace an agent proposal and shall provide a reason that remains linked to the original proposal and dissent.

The Resilience Decision Envelope shall bind the sealed case, every eligible and rejected agent output, dissent, arbitration, policy decision, approval, authorization, execution, validation, and outcome.

The system shall create a versioned Resilience Decision Envelope for every consequential recommendation or action. The envelope shall bind the normalized evidence, service and dependency context, graph revision, rule or model version, policy bundle, authorization, workflow, validation, and outcome by immutable identifiers and cryptographic digests.
Historical replay, omission, substitution, and integrity tests.
Signed decision-envelope manifest and successful independent reconstruction report.

The system shall bind every consequential recovery authorization to an explicit dependency-graph revision and shall re-evaluate, narrow, suspend, or invalidate the authorization when a material topology change affects target identity, blast radius, fallback validity, failure-domain independence, or required validation.
Graph delta, authorization transition, policy result, and reauthorization record.

The system shall issue a signed, short-lived, single-use bounded recovery authorization that identifies the provider-neutral action, permitted targets, tenant, environment, maximum scope, prerequisites, prohibited operations, expiry, compensation, validation plan, and exact provider-adapter translation. Adapters shall reject replay, target substitution, expired authority, and semantic expansion.
Cross-provider contract, replay, substitution, expiry, and confused-deputy tests.
Authorization envelope, adapter translation trace, nonce-consumption event, and provider result.

The system shall determine whether a service state is Qualified, Provisional, Unknown, or Disqualified from evidence sufficiency, provenance, freshness, consistency, observation-window completion, and required validation coverage. Missing or contradictory evidence shall not be silently treated as healthy.
Evidence loss, staleness, contradiction, and restoration tests.
Evidence Qualification Record, reason codes, state transition, and supporting lineage.

The system shall certify a primary and alternate recovery path only when graph analysis shows that the paths do not share prohibited correlated-failure domains, including regions, zones, clusters, control planes, identities, keys, networks, data stores, vendors, or upstream dependencies, subject to declared policy tolerances.
Correlated-failure graph fixtures and path-certification regression tests.
Recovery Path Certification with graph revision, disjointness evidence, exceptions, and expiry.

The system shall evaluate an ordered Cross-Layer Validation Plan after recovery across infrastructure, platform, application, data, security, AI behavior, SLO, and business-function checks. A failed mandatory check shall trigger the declared compensating action, rollback, containment, or escalation and shall prevent a successful recovery declaration.
Partial-recovery, false-positive, compensation, and rollback tests.
Validation-plan version, probe evidence, layer results, compensation history, and final recovery disposition.

A deployment enabling collaborative agents shall bind independently attributable proposals and dissent to qualified evidence, a graph revision, a policy version, and bounded agent authority; apply deterministic non-majority arbitration; preserve material dissent; and couple selection to separate bounded authorization, execution, cross-layer validation, and reconstructable provenance. Core conformance does not require collaborative agents.
Stale-context, dissent, tie, prompt-injection, partial-agent, replay, unauthorized-tool, deterministic-arbitration, execution, and reconstruction tests.
Sealed case, signed proposals and dissent, Arbitration Record, bounded authorization, validation results, and decision envelope.

The production control plane shall meet an initial monthly availability objective of 99.9 percent, excluding approved maintenance, and shall not be placed in the synchronous request path of protected services.
Loss of the control plane shall not interrupt protected workloads. Consequential actions shall stop safely, local collectors shall buffer within policy, and manual runbooks shall remain usable.
Transactional configuration and approval state shall use an initial RPO of fifteen minutes or less and RTO of four hours or less; stricter regulated requirements shall override these defaults.
For 95 percent of valid streaming events under the certified load, normalization and Core rule evaluation shall complete within ten seconds of receipt, excluding source delay and approval time.

Interactive service, finding, and decision views shall return within two seconds at the 95th percentile under the certified concurrent-user load; bounded graph-impact queries shall return within five seconds.

For P0 and P1 services, catalog-to-graph projection lag shall remain at or below sixty seconds at the 95th percentile and full reconciliation shall complete at least every twenty-four hours; stricter customer policy may reduce either threshold.

At least 95 percent of mandatory production dependency relationships for certified P0 and P1 services shall have an owner, criticality, provenance, confidence, effective interval, failure behavior, and current evidence; unresolved mandatory gaps shall prevent certification.

One hundred percent of consequential graph results shall record a graph revision, action-relevant subgraph digest, query identifier, parameters, result digest, and witness paths and shall reproduce deterministically from retained context.

Neo4j shall meet the approved control-plane availability objective and, after restoration, shall not permit consequential automation until retained events are replayed, reconciliation succeeds, graph revision continuity is verified, and required recovery-path certifications are revalidated.
Backup, restore, replay, and recertification exercise.
The design shall scale connectors, ingestion, rule evaluation, graph queries, workflows, and evidence processing independently and shall publish certified capacity limits.
All human and workload access shall use federated identity, least privilege, short-lived credentials, tenant and environment scoping, and deny-by-default authorization.
Data shall be encrypted in transit and at rest with approved keys, secrets shall be stored in a managed secrets service, and sensitive values shall not appear in logs or evidence manifests.
Production action execution shall require distinct identities from discovery and telemetry collection, and no identity shall both propose and approve a high-risk action.
All configuration, rule, policy, graph, approval, workflow, model, and administrative changes shall create immutable, time-synchronized audit events attributable to an identity.
Collection shall be minimized to the operational purpose; classification, retention, residency, legal hold, redaction, and deletion policies shall apply to normalized evidence and references.

Every decision-relevant source and relationship shall publish freshness, completeness, validity, uniqueness, consistency, and provenance measures; failed measures shall affect confidence or produce Unknown.
External interfaces shall use versioned OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, OpenTelemetry, JSON Schema, CloudEvents where appropriate, and stable provider-adapter contracts.

Components shall expose health, metrics, logs, traces, version, configuration checksum, dependency status, and runbook links, and shall support zero- or low-downtime upgrade where technically feasible.
Rules, policies, adapters, workflows, graph queries, schemas, and models shall have automated unit, contract, integration, replay, negative, security, and failure tests appropriate to their risk.
A trained operator shall be able to identify the decisive evidence, rule or model contribution, graph path, policy constraint, and expected action effect for every recommendation.
The operator portal shall meet WCAG 2.2 AA for supported workflows, including keyboard navigation, contrast, focus, labels, and non-color status communication.
Each UACRF component shall publish SLIs for availability, latency, errors, saturation, queue age, freshness, projection lag, workflow age, evidence failures, and dependency health.

Provider-specific logic shall remain within adapters; the decision core shall operate on canonical contracts and shall support at least AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud mappings described in the appendices.
The platform shall attribute ingestion, storage, graph, workflow, and model costs by tenant or service where feasible and shall support quotas, sampling, retention tiers, and cost alerts.

The product shall instrument onboarding lead time, manual touch time, exception rate, reusable mapping rate, evidence automation, and time to first accepted outcome by customer, provider, and service tier.
No externally visible claim shall be generated from an unsupported, expired, draft, contradictory, or out-of-scope assessment, model, certification, benchmark, or customer result.
Entitlement, billing, and product packaging failures shall not bypass tenant isolation, safety policy, evidence retention, workflow compensation, or customer data disposition obligations.

Every generally available capability shall have a named product owner, engineering owner, operational owner, security owner, support owner, documentation owner, deprecation policy, and funded maintenance plan.
Two qualified assessors applying the same pack to the same approved evidence produce the same categorical result or a documented, reviewable judgment difference.
Inter-rater calibration exercise and resolved variance log.
Every issued conclusion can be reconstructed from the engagement charter, pack version, scope, graph revision, workpapers, evidence, decisions, reviews, and approvals.
Missing, stale, weak, contradictory, and excluded evidence cannot silently produce a passing result or inflated confidence.
Sampling decisions are reproducible and failed samples trigger the published expansion rule.
Population, sample, selection, failure, and expansion test.
Criticality, severity, priority, confidence, residual risk, and conclusion rules operate consistently across supported packs and disclose approved differences.
Customer factual challenge, independent quality review, correction, reissuance, withdrawal, expiration, and reassessment preserve history and authority separation.
Assessment outputs state intended use, limitations, validity, evidence cutoff, uncertainty, and prohibited claims clearly enough for the target audience.
Report usability, legal-claims, and assurance review.
The methodology can be executed manually from controlled templates and through UACRF Assess without changing substantive results.

Manifest, excerpts, source hashes and locator checks

Invalidation, blocked stale reuse and retained history

Unknown disposition and explicit source limitations

Reservation ledger and bounded denied requests

Immutable terminal outcomes and rejection reasons

source_row_verbatim: At A2 the system shall collect advisory outputs for human review without automatic operational proposal selection, approval, qualification or provider execution; A3 arbitration shall require separate promotion.

Grant revocation and independently governed manual continuation

Version-bound evaluation pack and promotion or rollback disposition

source_json_specification_verbatim: The platform shall register each protected agent workload with a tenant, environment, service identity, accountable owner, runtime principal, intended purpose and workload kind.

The platform shall bind each execution to an immutable workload version containing model, instruction, knowledge, tool, memory, data and evaluation contracts, and shall require a new version for a material change.

The platform shall retain qualified and version-bound agent dependencies, including tool effects, identity, model, knowledge, memory, runtime and handoff dependencies, without treating topology alone as proof of eligibility or recovery independence.
The platform shall enforce authenticated scoped admission, a deadline and atomic per-attempt limits for steps, tokens and cost before runtime dispatch, including each parallel child.

The platform shall retain an attributed append-only event stream and shall return the original receipt for an identical source key and content while rejecting a conflicting reuse without a second budget debit.

The platform shall isolate sensitive memory and checkpoint artifacts by authorized scope and shall bind an eligible checkpoint to verified bytes, the workload version, input digest, event sequence, namespace and expiry.

The platform shall fence cancellation and pause requests at admission and dispatch, preserve late output without accepting it as eligible, and reconcile uncertain external effects before retry or resumption.

The platform shall require the existing governed recovery authority chain for consequential agent recovery and shall bind the recovery workflow to the exact source execution, checkpoint, evaluation and target version without granting recovery authority to the agent.

The platform shall stage resumption as a new linked execution with no greater remaining budget or deadline and shall reject stale evaluation, expired checkpoint, unresolved effects or incompatible context.

The platform shall assess agent recovery against a versioned mandatory evaluation suite and qualified observations of task, data, security and business outcomes, preserving FAIL or UNKNOWN when required checks are absent.
The platform shall preserve agent execution, context, tool effect, handoff, evaluation and recovery lineage in its decision evidence and shall retain a governed human continuation route.

The platform shall distinguish runtime reservations, measured provider usage and customer charges, correlate child attempts, prevent duplicate receipt charges and preserve safety controls when billing is unavailable.
